---
title: "Statistics for Biologists"
subtitle: "From study design to models that answer biological questions"
---

The statistics a working biologist actually needs — taught in R, with every example drawn from biology. Assumes the basic R from the companion course; the focus here is the statistics.

**New here? Start with [Choosing the Right Test](choosing-a-test.qmd)** — the decision guide for picking the correct analysis.

## The six parts

| Part | Focus |
|---|---|
| [I — Data & Description](PartI-theory.qmd) | study design, pseudoreplication, descriptive stats, exploratory plots |
| [II — Probability & Inference](PartII-theory.qmd) | distributions, sampling, the CLT, confidence intervals |
| [III — Hypothesis Testing](PartIII-theory.qmd) | p-values done right, t-tests & non-parametric, categorical data |
| [IV — Linear Models](PartIV-theory.qmd) | correlation, regression, ANOVA — one framework |
| [V — GLMs & Mixed Models](PartV-theory.qmd) | logistic & Poisson GLMs, mixed-effects models, model selection |
| [VI — Multivariate & Reproducible](PartVI-theory.qmd) | PCA & clustering, power, multiple testing, reproducible practice |

## Setup

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "lme4", "lmerTest", "MASS", "car"))
```
